title: Second-glance candidate curation scratchpad
notes:
Quick summary:
Candidate: Elio Navarro — applying for Senior Inference Engineer
Interview loop: take-home + two interviews (system design, debugging)
High-level impression: thoughtful engineer, strong debugging instincts, borderline on system design scale for senior level.

Technical highlights:
- Take-home: walked through a memory-efficient KV caching shim; code readable, decent tests, but omitted concurrent update handling (race condition on cache miss). Explains tradeoffs well when prompted.
- System design: proposed sharded key-value cache keyed by model+prefix; good latency/throughput tradeoffs; missed an explicit eviction policy for multi-tenant fairness (we asked later and received reasonable answers).
- Debugging: excellent on-the-spot narrowing steps. Local repro strategy was pragmatic (synthetic latency tests, microbenchmarks). Clear about tools he'd use (perf, async stack traces, flamegraphs).
- Ops awareness: cares about observability; suggested concrete metrics (95th token latency, kv hit rate, request fanout) and alert thresholds.

Red flags / open concerns:
- Edge-case reasoning under load: tended to prefer simpler solutions without fully accounting for tail latency amplification in batched workloads. Needs prodding to push into worst-case scenarios.
- Concurrency: missing initial handling for races in take-home. Accepted as oversight but didn't volunteer a lock-free alternative; prefers coarse-grained locks which might not scale.
- Communication: clear in 1:1s, but in group conversations sometimes stops short of summarizing next steps. Might require coaching for cross-team syncs.

Culture & behavioral fit:
- Mentoring: positive signals — has run on-call rotations and mentored junior engineers at previous company.
- Tradeoffs: pragmatic; prioritizes shipping with observability rather than premature optimization.
- Trigger for growth: would benefit from exposure to multi-region routing and formalized SLO design patterns.

Proposal / recommendation:
- Recommend move to final hire conversation with PM + on-call scenario play (simulate incident triage).
- Rank: green for senior IC with a short onboarding plan to pair on high-concurrency paths and SLO exercises.
- Suggested compensation bucket: mid-range for senior (benchmark vs other offers).

Follow-ups & TODOs:
- Ask candidate to sketch eviction and fairness policy for multi-tenant KV cache (take-home follow-up, 30–45m remote session).
- Panel to probe concurrency: give a controlled race problem and ask for lock-free/optimistic solution sketch.
- Reference check: focus on system design depth and experience handling production tail latency.

Calibration notes (vs recent loop):
- Compared to candidate A (strong design lead) — Elio is more pragmatic and hands-on, slightly weaker on architecture framing.
- Compared to candidate B (strong on concurrency) — Elio better at debugging and observability.

Notes to myself:
- Keep this loose — want perspectives from Jonas and Priya before marking in Green/Yellow/Red in the official scorecard.
- If we move forward, schedule the on-call simulation within next 3 business days to keep momentum.

Raw chatter (scratch):
- liked: shipping mindset, observability-first
- meh: initial concurrency handling
- question: would he advocate for cache tiering vs model-side caching?
